items.front: Dynastic order of Magadha before the Mauryas?
items.back: Haryanka → Shishunaga → Nanda → Maurya.

items.front: Founder & capital of the Haryanka dynasty?
items.back: Bimbisara (effective founder); capital Rajagriha (Girivraja).

items.front: Which region did Bimbisara annex for trade?
items.back: Anga (capital Champa); he was a contemporary of Buddha & Mahavira.

items.front: Ajatashatru's two war engines against the Vajjis?
items.back: Mahashilakantaka (catapult) & Rathamusala (mace-fitted chariot).

items.front: Who convened the First Buddhist Council, and where?
items.back: Ajatashatru, at Rajagriha, after Buddha's Parinirvana.

items.front: Who founded Pataliputra and where?
items.back: Udayin, at the Ganga–Son confluence (modern Patna).

items.front: Shishunaga dynasty — capital shift and key conquest?
items.back: Shifted capital to Vaishali; annexed Avanti, ending the long rivalry.

items.front: Who held the Second Buddhist Council, and where?
items.back: Kalasoka (Kakavarna), at Vaishali.

items.front: Founder of the Nanda dynasty and his titles?
items.back: Mahapadma Nanda — Ugrasena, Ekarat, Sarva-kshatrantaka; first non-Kshatriya empire.

items.front: Which Nanda king was Alexander's contemporary (326 BCE)?
items.back: Dhana Nanda (Greek: Agrammes/Xandrames); had the Nandopakramani standard.

items.front: Mahapadma Nanda's famous conquest linked to Hathigumpha?
items.back: Kalinga — later referenced in Kharavela's Hathigumpha inscription.

items.front: Who overthrew Dhana Nanda and when?
items.back: Chandragupta Maurya with Chanakya, c. 321 BCE.

items.front: What emerged from the constant wars between the Mahajanapadas?
items.back: Magadha, as the largest empire.
items.examPoint: Order of Magadha dynasties (Haryanka → Shishunaga → Nanda → Maurya)

items.front: Vedic and Buddhist textual sources on the Mahajanapadas?
items.back: Vedic: the Brahmanas and Upanishads. Buddhist: the Vinaya, Sutta and Abhidhamma Pitakas.
items.examPoint: Sources — Vedic/Buddhist/Jain texts, NBPW pottery, Hathigumpha inscription

items.front: Sites where NBPW pottery has been found?
items.back: Ahichchhatra, Hastinapur, Kausambi, Ujjaini and other sites.
items.examPoint: Sources — Vedic/Buddhist/Jain texts, NBPW pottery, Hathigumpha inscription

items.front: Haryanka founder and important rulers?
items.back: Founder debated — many credit Bimbisara's grandfather. Key rulers: Bimbisara, Ajatashatru, Udayin.
items.examPoint: Haryanka Dynasty — capital Rajagriha; founder debated

items.front: Why are the Haryankas called a parricide dynasty?
items.back: Kings killed their fathers to take the throne — Ajatashatru killed Bimbisara.
items.examPoint: Haryanka Dynasty — capital Rajagriha; founder debated

items.front: Reign dates: Bimbisara, Ajatashatru, Udayin?
items.back: Bimbisara 544–492 BCE; Ajatashatru 492–460 BCE; Udayin 460–444 BCE.
items.examPoint: Bimbisara — reign & contemporary of Buddha and Mahavira

items.front: Ajatashatru — rank in the dynasty and work at the capital?
items.back: The most powerful Haryanka ruler; he began to fortify Rajgriha.
items.examPoint: Ajatashatru's war engines & fortification of Rajgriha

items.front: Which republic besides the Vajjis did Ajatashatru defeat?
items.back: The Mallas.

items.front: Dates of the Shishunaga and Nanda dynasties?
items.back: Shishunaga c. 413–345 BCE; Nanda c. 345–321 BCE.
items.examPoint: Shishunaga Dynasty — origin under Nagadasaka, capital Vaishali, annexation of Avanti

items.front: When did the Second Buddhist Council meet?
items.back: About 100 years after the Buddha's death, c. 383 BCE, at Vaishali under Kalasoka.

items.front: Where did Kalasoka keep his capital?
items.back: He moved it back from Vaishali to Pataliputra.

items.front: Mahapadma Nanda's administrative record?
items.back: The first empire builder; an effective tax-collection system and irrigation canals.
items.examPoint: Mahapadma Nanda — Ugrasena, titles, Kalinga conquest, Navanandas

items.front: Dhana Nanda — place in the dynasty and reputation?
items.back: The last significant Nanda, with a vast army; unpopular for heavy taxation.
items.examPoint: Dhana Nanda — Agrammes/Xandrames, Nandopakramani, Alexander's invasion

items.front: Why did Alexander's army refuse to cross the Beas?
items.back: Partly from fear of the huge Nanda army of Magadha.
items.examPoint: Dhana Nanda — Agrammes/Xandrames, Nandopakramani, Alexander's invasion

items.front: Did Pataliputra remain the capital after the Nandas?
items.back: Yes — it remained the imperial capital under the Nandas and the Mauryas.
items.examPoint: Transition from the Nandas to the Mauryas
